title: Plugin scope ruling 28: managed decides over every scope and a managed deciding row is never updated
description: Binding record: opum-doc main 7818aca8b, docs/adr/distribute-lore-and-quest-agent-skills-through-the-plugin-marketplace.md, Amendment 6 (ODOC-286, commit 44326c508, opum-ai/opum-doc#458), ruling 28. Read it there before implementing. The full scope order is managed > local > project > user > synced. This supersedes ruling 26(ii) for managed only: managed decides ahead of the rest when present and applicable (Claude Code's own code treats a managed row as applicable to every project, as it does user). A managed deciding row is NEVER updated: no '--scope managed' update runs (Claude Code itself refuses with 'Cannot install plugins to managed scope'); state is reported with scope 'managed', and the remedy names the administrator's managed settings in prose, not a command the user can run. lore-cli owes this because dc09ca98 (LCLI-592, opum-ai/lore-cli#291) implements ruling 26's order. Per the orchestrator's 2026-09-26 agreement, this task owns everything managed: the detection precedence in src/core/agent-plugins.ts / src/adapters/agent-plugins.ts AND the update guard in LCLI-593's --target --force update path. Ruling 29 (the deepest-projectPath tie-break within one scope) is already implemented by dc09ca98 and is now binding; keep it. A managed row's real rendering is unmeasured on any install (Amendment 6 provenance), so tests use recorded outputs built from the schema Amendment 6 measured.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Detection orders scopes managed > local > project > user > synced, so an applicable managed row decides over every other scope (including a project-matching local row), proven by tests over recorded list outputs with managed enabled and managed disabled

A managed deciding row is never updated: lore agents --target claude --force runs no update against it, reports scope managed with update not-run, and its remedy is prose naming the administrator managed settings, not a runnable command; proven through a stub runtime that logs every call
Ruling 29 (deepest projectPath within one scope) still holds, and docs (cli-surface, cli-contract, lore instructions agents) state the order; bun test and bun run lore check exit 0

implementationNotes: AGREED 2026-09-26 with quest-cli (QCLI-381), binding under ruling (d) without the orchestrator (opum-agent 94d64804 delegated exactly this: 'a string you both agree on binds'). quest-cli proposed and lore-cli replied 'agreed'. Whenever the deciding Claude row has scope managed, in installed or disabled state alike, the remedy is EXACTLY: 'managed by your Claude Code administrator: opum-lore@opum is set in the managed settings, which only an administrator can change'. quest's string is byte-identical except for the plugin id (opum-quest@opum). Behaviour: the state keeps its usual value; scope 'managed' is reported; '--scope managed' never appears in a remedy or in argv; 'lore agents --target claude --force' runs only the list and reports update 'not-run' with this remedy. Order managed > local > project > user > synced; within one scope the deepest projectPath decides (ruling 29, already in dc09ca98); a managed row has no projectPath and applies everywhere. Deliberate: ONE string for both states (a per-state variant invites a runnable-looking one) and NO filesystem path (the managed-settings location differs by OS and is unmeasured).

IMPLEMENTED on branch feat/LCLI-604-managed-scope (implementer specialist, isolated worktree). Binding record read at opum-doc main b4368735 through the GitHub contents API (the isolation harness refused reading the sibling checkout), Amendment 6 rulings 28 and 29. (1) updateDetail for a managed INSTALLED deciding row is EXACTLY 'the deciding row is managed by your Claude Code administrator, so it is never updated' -- quest-cli proposed it for QCLI-381, lore-cli agreed it byte-for-byte 2026-09-26 under ruling (d); exported as MANAGED_SCOPE_UPDATE_DETAIL beside MANAGED_SCOPE_REMEDY in src/core/agent-plugins.ts, both pinned by literal. (2) Managed rows are EXEMPT from the projectPath filter whether or not they carry one, and their projectPath is never compared, so they never enter the ruling 29 depth tie-break -- parity with quest-cli. Precedence is now managed > local > project > user > synced (src/adapters/agent-plugins.ts). lorePluginUpdateSteps(claude, managed) returns no argv and the adapter update runs nothing on empty steps, a second guard behind updateLorePlugin. (3) Tests in test/agent-plugins.test.ts. AC1: 'ruling 28: the full precedence is managed > local > project > user > synced, in either row order'; 'managed ENABLED decides over a project-matching DISABLED local row and every other scope, in either order'; 'managed DISABLED decides over a project-matching ENABLED local row and every other scope, in either order'; 'a managed row applies to every project: one WITH a non-matching projectPath still decides'. AC2 via the lore agents command path, a logging stub port over the real adapter and a recorded runner: '--target claude --force on managed INSTALLED: only the list runs, update not-run, the agreed detail and prose remedy'; '--target claude --force on managed DISABLED: only the list runs, the disabled not-run path, still the managed remedy'; '--plain and pretty say the same, and never introduce the managed remedy as a command'; '--target claude --check: the managed remedy for installed and disabled alike, and nothing runs'; 'a bare lore agents --force: managed installed is not-run with the managed detail, not a --target promise'; and the subprocess case against a fake claude that logs every invocation, 'ruling 28 (LCLI-604): a managed deciding row under --target claude --force starts the list command only' (log equals exactly the one list command). AC3: 'ruling 29 still holds, and a managed row never enters the depth tie-break against local rows', with the pre-existing ruling 26(ii) depth tests unchanged and green. (4) Mutation: managed moved back to 4th in CLAUDE_SCOPE_PRECEDENCE gave 11 of 101 red in test/agent-plugins.test.ts (exactly the tests whose listing pairs managed with another scope) and 90 green; the literal-pin test and the no-scope-managed-argv test ran and stayed green. Restored: 101 of 101. Gates: bun run lint exit 0 (3 warnings and 1 info, all in untouched files), typecheck exit 0, full bun test exit 0 (3653 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail, 111 files), bun run lore check exit 0 (82 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings).

REVIEW FIXES on eac5586a (adversarial review, nothing blocking), in a second commit on feat/LCLI-604-managed-scope. S2: cli-surface's bare lore agents --force sentence now carries the managed exception in the same sentence (managed prose remedy; managed updateDetail when installed). N2: the test formerly named 'a managed row never enters the depth tie-break against local rows' is renamed to 'ruling 29 still holds among local rows, and a managed row decides over them whatever projectPath it carries', with a comment saying what it cannot see; the managed-vs-managed depth question is not pinned. N3: decodeClaudePluginList now reads the scope through core's printable() (now exported), the same form checkFromListing compares to managed, so a padded 'managed ' is ranked AND treated as managed -- fail-safe, nothing runs. The other choice was rejected because core would have seen 'managed' after trimming while the decoder ranked it unknown. Tests: 'a padded managed scope (managed ) is ranked AND treated as managed, so it decides and nothing is offered to run' and 'a padded managed scope under --target claude --force: only the list runs, and no --scope managed anywhere'. Mutation: decoder back to the raw scope -> exactly those 2 of 105 red. N4: the adapter comment no longer claims user-row parity. N5: cli-surface and the adapter comment now say the deciding row is chosen by scope precedence, then projectPath depth within a scope. NEW RULE, opum-agent ruling 2026-09-26 (disabled wins among managed rows); opum-doc ruling-28 amendment pending: among two or more applicable managed rows for one plugin id, any disabled one makes the state disabled whatever the list order, and only-enabled reports installed. Implemented in the decoder's selection (decidesOver), not by sorting; ruling 29 is unchanged for the other scopes. Clause added to cli-surface, cli-contract and the lore instructions agents topic. Tests: 'disabled wins among managed rows: two applicable managed rows, one disabled, report disabled in either order' and 'disabled wins among managed rows: two ENABLED managed rows report installed, and another plugin's disabled managed row does not count'. Mutation: rule removed -> exactly 1 of 105 red, failing on the enabled-then-disabled order (reported installed). S1 still ON HOLD, unchanged. Gates: bun run lint exit 0; biome check on the 4 changed TS files exit 0; typecheck exit 0; full bun test exit 0 (3657 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail, 111 files); bun run lore check exit 0 (82 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings).
finalSummary: Delivered in opum-ai/lore-cli#305 (CI pull_request run 36271531155, success on e4f04db1, all 13 jobs green). Claude plugin scope precedence is now managed > local > project > user > synced (ruling 28). A managed row applies to every project whatever its projectPath, and among managed rows disabled wins in any list order (opum-agent ruling 2026-09-26; opum-doc ruling-28 amendment pending at close). A managed deciding row is never updated: no update argv is built, and --scope managed never appears. It reports scope managed and update not-run, with the ruling-(d) strings agreed with quest-cli: remedy "managed by your Claude Code administrator: opum-lore@opum is set in the managed settings, which only an administrator can change" and installed updateDetail "the deciding row is managed by your Claude Code administrator, so it is never updated". Ruling 29 holds for the other scopes. Docs: lore instructions agents, cli-surface and cli-contract. An adversarial review found nothing blocking, and its S2 and N2-N5 are applied. S1 (the updateDetail on a managed DISABLED row) needs quest-cli parity and is filed as LCLI-608.
